verdict: Paid ads went dark this week; relaunch is blocked on setup gaps being closed now.
narrative: Both Meta and Google ads came to a complete stop on September 17th and have run at zero spend through this week — this was an abrupt halt, not a gradual decline, and all new paid lead flow paused with it. The 28-day totals (102 leads at $16.02 per lead) reflect the three solid weeks before that stop and do not represent current activity. Ads are not being restarted until key infrastructure items are verified — specifically, payment paths and conversion tracking — so that budget is not running into an unconfirmed system. Once those items are confirmed, paid campaigns will relaunch; next week's report should show spend resuming and lead flow returning.

highlights.phrase: leads received over the last 28 days, all generated before ads paused on September 17th
cost per lead over the 28-day window, across $1,634 in total ad spend
consecutive days with zero ad spend on both Meta and Google as of this report

watch_item.issue: Both paid channels are dark and no leads are being generated in real time; the stop is tied to unverified payment and conversion tracking infrastructure that must be confirmed before relaunch.
watch_item.fix: Verification of payment paths and conversion tracking is underway this week, with a target completion by September 30th — ads resume once those checks pass.
